newsitem.title: FRANCE: Arafat wants Europeans in talks with Israelis.
newsitem.headline: Arafat wants Europeans in talks with Israelis.

text.p: Palestinian President Yasser Arafat called on Friday for a European presence in talks scheduled to start between Palestinian and Israeli officials on Sunday.

"We want an effective European role in the consolidation of the peace process in the Middle East and a European presence in future meetings with the Israelis, the first of which is to take place on Sunday (on the Israel-Gaza border)," Arafat told reporters after talks with French President Jacques Chirac.

Arafat, standing with Chirac on the steps of the Elysee presidential palace, said peace in the Middle East was as important to the world at large as to Israelis and Palestinians. Some 58 Arabs and 15 Jews have died in fighting since last week.

Chirac telephoned Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to brief him on his talks with Arafat but did not mention the suggestion for European participation, Chirac's spokewoman Catherine Colonna said.

She declined to say what France's position was on the issue, telling reporters to wait until a European Union summit in Dublin on Saturday. Paris had criticised Washington for failing to invite European leaders to a Middle East summit this week.
Chirac said earlier that EU leaders were expected to call for an active role in reviving the Middle East peace process.

Arafat and Chirac met for 90 minutes after the Palestinian president's arrival from Italy, where he briefed government leaders on his emergency summit in Washington with Netanyahu on Tuesday and Wednesday.
"I am not asking for the impossible. I want the application of the accords which I reached with them (Israel) which were not bilateral but international agreements," Arafat said.
"Those accords will consolidate peace and security is peace. There is no security without peace. That is why I ask President Chirac to transmit this message to the European Union".
In Dublin, Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring said: "The European Union has a major role to play in the Middle East process and I'm sure that will be reflected in the discussion tomorrow.
"What is important is that the European Union will have to fit in with the negotiations (between Israel and the Palestinians)."

The French leader said U.S. President Bill Clinton was right to call a Palestinian-Israeli summit in Washington in a bid to get the peace process back on track "but what is now needed are strong acts".
"I naturally understand Israel's security needs but security cannot be guaranteed by force," said Chirac.

"It is essential that the peace process resume...I hope that the forthcoming (Palestinian-Israeli) meeting at Erez will allow the peace process to resume," he said. Arafat later left Paris for Cairo, airport officials said.
Earlier on Friday, France sniped at Washington for the scant results of the two-day Middle East summit.

"A meeting prepared in other conditions would have allowed concrete results," Foreign Ministry spokesman Jacques Rummelhardt said of the summit at the White House that ended with no breakthroughs apart from a deal to keep talking.
